body: This works as designed (and required by the spec). For a normal scoped bean a client proxy is used instead of the contextual instance for injection, observers notification, etc. So the no-args constructor is first called when instantiating the proxy (which is a subclass of `FooBean`) and then for the contextual instance. It's a good practice to use a `@PostConstruct` callback to initialize the bean. Also if your bean declares a bean constructor with parameters (injection points) you would not observe this behavior either (client proxy is always instantiated via the noa-args constructor). Another solution is to switch to `@Singleton` or `@Dependent` for which a client proxy is not created at all.
In fact, I was wrong! Client proxies should not be used for observers. I'll try to fix it next week.

body: I've sent a [PR](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/pull/8087) that partially fixes you problem. However, note that the no-args constructor will be called once a client proxy is needed, i.e. when the bean is injected somewhere. This is a well-known limitation of CDI.
The issue does not seem to be fixed in version 1.9.2 of Quarkus. The no args constructor is called twice when using the Startup annotation even though the bean is not inject anywhere.

> The issue does not seem to be fixed in version 1.9.2 of Quarkus. 

So first of all it not an issue but a well known limitation as described above. Even if we don't create a client proxy for an observer it will be created once the bean is actually used (upon the first method invocation).

> The no args constructor is called twice when using the Startup annotation even though the bean is not inject anywhere.

A contextual instance is also created if you obtain a bean via `CDI.current()` and programmatic lookup. Could it be the case?

> A contextual instance is also created if you obtain a bean via CDI.current() and programmatic lookup. Could it be the case?

I don't think so. When I only add: `void startup(@Observes StartupEvent event) {} ` to the application scoped class, then the constructor is only called once. When I add `@Startup`instead, then the constructor is called twice.

> When I add @Startup instead, then the constructor is called twice.

I see. You're actually right, for `@Startup` we obtain the bean instance via `Arc.container().instance(bean)`, so the client proxy is involved. We could modify the code to access the contextual instance directly. However, it's not a big win (for the reasons mentioned above).

>  However, it's not a big win (for the reasons mentioned above).

I agree. I cannot judge if it is worth the effort.
